stories.notes: Stub story with empty acceptance criteria and null spec spanning three platforms (GO, UP, MX) for live preview in CMS. Openspec must elaborate requirements and define scope across all three systems; speckit must then harden testability, security, and edge cases. High priority due to cross-platform complexity and complete absence of elaborated requirements.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — Live Preview integration with Contentstack CMS. No existing fix site; the work attaches into the central content context and its consumer hook. VCs derived entirely from description since ACs are empty. Criteria stop at our side of the Contentstack API boundary.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria, so all criteria are new. I examined the actual codebase to ground them: (1) contentstackContext.tsx exports only a context object and interface — no provider component, so Live Preview integration must supply a provider that wraps the app and manages state. (2) useContent.ts exposes getContentByKey via getValue — Live Preview must ensure merged data is accessible through this existing API. (3) The mock data reveals Contentstack entry shapes including rich-text docs (type:'doc', children, uid), modular blocks with Cloudinary images, and metadata fields (_version, publish_details) — AC-9 and AC-10 ensure these nested structures survive the merge. (4) No @contentstack/live-preview-sdk package is currently installed, so AC-5 guards against bad initialization config. (5) AC-2 is the critical regression guard: production behavior must be unchanged. AC-6 and AC-12 address error resilience and race conditions respectively. AC-7 ensures cross-content-type isolation. AC-8 covers session teardown. I could not locate the provider component or page-level integration point — the context file only defines the shape — so these ACs are written against the observable behavior of the context + hook contract, not a specific provider file.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value. Openspec derived 7 verification criteria from an empty brownfield stub, covering initialization, re-rendering, backward compatibility, cross-brand behavior, hook contract stability, malformed-data resilience, and SDK config correctness. Speckit then grounded the criteria in the actual codebase: it correctly identified that contentstackContext.tsx exports only a context object and interface (no provider component — confirmed by reading the file), that useContent.ts reads via useContext + getValue (confirmed), that no @contentstack/live-preview-sdk package is installed, and that mock data reveals nested Contentstack entry shapes. Speckit's observation that it could not locate a provider component is accurate and correctly scoped — the context file contains only createContext. The fixSiteAnalysis is plausible: the primary attachment point is contentstackContext.tsx (wrapping with a LivePreviewProvider) and useContent.ts automatically propagates changes once the context updates. All 5 manifest paths verified as exact matches. Verification criteria are observable and testable (mocked onEntryChange, query-parameter flag, cross-brand context, existing consumers unchanged, malformed entry handling). The detective plan mentioned useContent and Contentstack provider/init as targets; the fixSiteAnalysis found contentstackContext.tsx and useContent.ts — the plan terms overlap with finding terms and the reasoning connects naturally (trace useContent → context → provider). No unexplained pivot. Ordinary open questions remain (where the new provider component file lives, how server-side preview hash parameters flow), but these are implementation details a competent writer resolves.
